clue.text: Make rough trip in one's car

indicators.note: a trip is a stumble, so these letters stumble into a new order

parts.note: the letters of these words, the possessive counted as its S

explanation.surface: A bumpy journey in your own car shakes everything up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trip' reads as a journey but signals the anagram of ONESCAR.
explanation.definitionFit: To make something rough is to give it a cruder, harsher texture, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Bird, fish, and insect

parts.note: a cock is a male bird
a roach is a freshwater fish

explanation.surface: A list of three creatures.
explanation.definitionFit: A scuttling household pest, a common example of an insect.

clue.text: State — a revolutionary Balkan one, without monarch

indicators.note: revolutionary means the letters are turned about into a new order
without means a letter is removed from Balkan

parts.note: K is the abbreviation for king
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A Balkan state with a revolutionary past and no king.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface invites a Balkan revolution; 'without monarch' is a deletion of K for king, and 'revolutionary' mixes what is left with I, all after A.
explanation.definitionFit: A Balkan country, a nation state on the Adriatic.

clue.text: Game that's so inferior his interest's ending

parts.note: low means inferior

indicators.note: ending means the final letter of interest's

explanation.surface: A game so poor that he loses interest.
explanation.definitionFit: A card game related to whist in which a player may bid to win tricks alone.

clue.text: Unsophisticated fare succeeded in foreign theatre

indicators.note: in means one piece goes inside another

parts.note: Noh is classical Japanese theatre
S is the abbreviation for succeeded, as in family trees

explanation.surface: Plain food was a hit at an overseas theatre.
explanation.walkthrough: NOSH is British slang for food.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang for food, simple grub rather than haute cuisine.

clue.text: Pick-up point where unromantic teacher meets head

definitions.text: Pick-up point where unromantic teacher meets head

parts.words: Pick-up point where unromantic teacher meets head
parts.note: a pick-up sounds like a romantic encounter, but here it is merely the spot a vehicle collects passengers, where a teacher might run into the headteacher

explanation.surface: A dull schoolteacher has an assignation with the headteacher.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pick-up' suggests romance; 'unromantic' warns that it means passengers being picked up, and 'head' is the headteacher waiting in the same queue. Some may also see BUSS (a kiss) meeting TOP (head), but the kiss is far from unromantic.
explanation.definitionFit: Buses pick up passengers at a fixed roadside stopping place.

clue.text: Naval flag produced by navy officer

parts.note: navy is a shade of blue
an ensign is a junior officer

explanation.surface: A naval flag designed by a navy officer.
explanation.definitionFit: A flag flown by British naval auxiliary and certain yacht clubs' vessels.

clue.text: It links the South of France and an African country

parts.note: sud is French for south

explanation.surface: Something connects the Riviera with an African nation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the South of France' is not the Riviera but the French word for south; 'It links' and 'and' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: A nation in north-east Africa on the Nile.

clue.text: People's champion finds supportive member in sympathy

indicators.note: in means one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: tune as in 'in tune', in sympathy or agreement
a rib supports the body's frame

explanation.surface: A people's champion shows a sympathetic member.
explanation.walkthrough: In ancient Rome a tribune was an official protecting plebeians' interests.
explanation.definitionFit: A Roman official elected to protect the plebeians, hence any popular defender.

clue.text: Bishop, for one, brings some food to church

parts.note: a pie is some food
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A bishop brings a dish to church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bishop' is a chess man, not a cleric.
explanation.definitionFit: A chessman: the bishop is an example of a chess figure.

clue.text: Clique initially formed by chance

parts.note: the famous clique of Charles II's ministers had initials that happened to spell an existing word for a secret faction

explanation.surface: A little group of friends came together by accident.
explanation.walkthrough: Charles II's ministers Clifford, Arlington, Buckingham, Ashley and Lauderdale had initials that by coincidence spelt this existing word, so the clique was 'initially formed by chance'.
explanation.definitionFit: A secret political faction or intriguing clique, the very sense the ministers' initials happened to give.

clue.text: Brief but memorable passage from channel to bay, say

parts.note: a sound is a narrow sea channel

indicators.note: say tells us the next word is to be taken by how it is spoken

parts.note: a bight is a wide curving bay

explanation.surface: A short sea passage from a channel to a bay.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is all geography; 'passage' is a quotable snippet of speech, not a sea route.
explanation.definitionFit: A pithy extract from a speech or interview that is quoted widely on air.

clue.text: Celebrity in divorce centre rejected new wife

parts.note: Reno, Nevada was famous for quick divorces

indicators.note: rejected means the pair of letters for new and wife are sent back, read right to left

explanation.surface: A famous person at a divorce venue has dumped the new spouse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejected' turns NW round to WN after RENO.
explanation.definitionFit: Celebrity in the sense of fame: being widely known and acclaimed.

clue.text: Provide even more cover for controller? Certainly!

parts.note: a rein controls a horse
sure means certainly, as in 'Sure!'

explanation.surface: An insurance query met by an emphatic yes.
explanation.definitionFit: Insurers pass on risk by taking out further cover with another underwriter.

clue.text: Part of watch that was very cold for Mimi

definitions.meaning: the long pointer on a clock face

definitions.text: that was very cold for Mimi
definitions.meaning: in La Bohème Rodolfo sings that Mimi's tiny hand is frozen

explanation.walkthrough: Puccini's aria 'Che gelida manina' tells of Mimi's tiny, frozen hand.
explanation.definitionFit: The long pointer on a clock dial; read also as a tiny palm, as in the opera.

clue.text: You can count on them getting transport back into capital

indicators.note: into means one piece is put inside the other

parts.note: A1 means first-rate or capital, written here with the 1 as letter I

indicators.note: back tells us the transport word is read in reverse

parts.note: a cab is transport

explanation.surface: Taking a ride back into the capital city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns CAB to BAC, which goes into AI (A1, 'capital' in the sense of excellent).
explanation.definitionFit: Counting frames with beads, the plural of the bead-frame calculator.

clue.text: On the rocks near Southampton, with five on board

indicators.note: on board means one thing is carried within another

parts.note: in the Solent, the strait off Southampton
V is the Roman numeral five

explanation.surface: A boat runs aground near Southampton with five people aboard.
explanation.walkthrough: The Solent is the strait between Southampton and the Isle of Wight; V goes into IN SOLENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Bankrupt, like a marriage or business said to be on the rocks.

clue.text: Become engaged to secure some brass

parts.note: to lock is to secure
horns are brass instruments

explanation.surface: A couple get engaged to buy brass instruments.
explanation.walkthrough: 'engaged' means in conflict, not betrothed.
explanation.definitionFit: To clash in combat, as stags do, so engaged in a fight.

clue.text: Reflect on changes in musical notation

indicators.note: changes signals that these letters alter their order

explanation.surface: Thinking about variation in how music is written.
explanation.definitionFit: A symbol on the stave fixing pitch for tenor ranges.

clue.text: Crippled and unskilful player put on line

parts.note: a ham is a poor overacting performer
strung means threaded on a string or line

explanation.surface: A clumsy actor gets injured and laid out.
explanation.definitionFit: Hamstrung means disabled or hampered, originally by cutting the leg tendon.

clue.text: Close to crash, for example, coming out of Lyme Regis

indicators.note: crash means the remaining letters smash into a new order
coming out of means some letters are taken away from the place name

explanation.surface: A car crash near a Dorset seaside town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coming out of' takes EG from LYMEREGIS, and 'crash' rearranges LYMRIS. Lyme Regis is a Dorset seaside town.
explanation.definitionFit: Close means stingy, tight with money.

clue.text: Having driven dangerously asked to be excused?

definitions.meaning: pulled sharply in front of another vehicle
at a dance, a partner is taken over with an 'excuse me', interrupting a couple

explanation.walkthrough: 'Having' is a link: 'Having driven dangerously' gives the past participle.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase covers overtaking and swerving into a lane, and also interrupting a dancing couple to claim a partner.

clue.text: In counting house, there's 28!

parts.note: a tally is a count

explanation.surface: In a counting house, someone spots something.
explanation.walkthrough: 28 across is the fox; this is the huntsman's cry on sighting one.
explanation.definitionFit: The hunting cry raised on sighting the fox.

clue.text: Put into office, having been elected, say, by 500

parts.note: in means elected, as in 'voted in'
to state is to say
D is the Roman numeral 500

explanation.surface: A politician takes office after winning by 500 votes.
explanation.definitionFit: Installed formally in a position or role.

clue.text: Gather from a certain fertile allotment

indicators.note: an allotment is a portion, so a portion of these words is taken

explanation.surface: Drawing conclusions from a fertile garden plot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'allotment' looks like a garden plot but signals a share of 'certain fertile'.
explanation.definitionFit: To deduce or conclude, as in 'I gather you agree'.

clue.text: Ruler of Queen's Navee was never so perplexed

definitions.text: Ruler of Queen's Navee was never so
definitions.meaning: Sir Joseph Porter in HMS Pinafore became ruler of the navy though he never went to sea

explanation.walkthrough: Gilbert and Sullivan's HMS Pinafore has Sir Joseph boast he 'never went to sea'.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom for bewildered; literally afloat on the ocean, which Sir Joseph never was.

clue.text: Bad feeling produced by arrest, we hear

indicators.note: we hear tells us the word is picked by how it is spoken

parts.note: to collar is to arrest

explanation.surface: Being detained by police causes resentment.
explanation.definitionFit: Anger or irritability, from the old humour yellow bile.

clue.text: Sound head needed for political group

indicators.note: Sound tells us the word is judged by how it is spoken

parts.note: block is slang for head, as in 'knock your block off'

explanation.surface: A sensible leader is what a party needs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sound' reads as sensible but signals the homophone.
explanation.definitionFit: An alliance of nations or parties acting together.

clue.text: Head off in direction of East stand

parts.note: for means towards, as in 'heading for'
a stall is a market stand

explanation.surface: Someone heads off towards the east stand at a ground.
explanation.definitionFit: To prevent something by acting first, intercepting it.

clue.text: Magnificent little chaps

parts.note: Roy and Al are short men's names
Al is a short man's name

explanation.surface: Praise for some splendid small boys.
explanation.walkthrough: 'little chaps' gives two short male names side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: Regal, splendid, fit for a monarch.

clue.text: Hunted creature fled back into drey in confusion

indicators.note: into means one piece goes inside another
in confusion means the letters of drey are jumbled
back means the word for fled is read right to left

parts.note: ran means fled

explanation.surface: A hunted squirrel bolts home to its nest in a panic.
explanation.walkthrough: A drey is a squirrel's nest, which makes the surface picture a squirrel; the hunted creature is really the fox of fable.
explanation.definitionFit: The fox's name in medieval fable, the quarry of the hunt.

clue.text: Start journey with an empty stage?

definitions.meaning: a boat sets off by untying its moorings
a play's actors, all removed, would leave the stage bare

explanation.definitionFit: Untie a vessel and set sail; also read as the cast being off the stage.
